subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Peak-End Rule
description: A 60-second lesson on The Peak-End Rule.

hook.text: A painful medical procedure ending gently is remembered as less painful than a shorter, sharper one.

buildup.text: Kahneman's peak-end rule: we judge experiences by their most intense moment and how they ended.

discovery.text: Duration barely matters. A 30-minute ordeal with a gentle end beats a 10-minute one with a harsh end.

twist.text: Disney knows this: the fireworks are at the end. Your last memory is the one that sticks.

climax.text: This splits us into two selves: the experiencing self who lives it and the remembering self who judges it.

punchline.text: End well. That's what gets remembered.

quiz.question: What does the peak-end rule predict?
options: We judge experiences by peak intensity and ending
Duration is the key factor in memory
